title: Graves Blanc
notes: Green-gold and crystalline. Citrus, white flowers and a touch of honey.
pairing: Prawns from the plancha.
sommelier_note: Half Sauvignon, forty percent Sémillon and a splash of Muscadelle from the Graves: fresh, elegant and very easy to pour.

title: Pessac-Léognan Rouge
notes: Red and blackberry fruit, silky oak and grippy tannin with a long finish.
pairing: Roast lamb, duck breast or a hard cheese.
drink_window: Mid-term drinking: now and over the next few years
sommelier_note: Six hectares of sand and fine white gravel that share their geology with the Grands Crus, farmed partly with horses by Philippe and Chantal Miecaze.

title: Pessac-Léognan Rouge
notes: Powerful black fruit with a little oak. Charming, generous, soft tannin and good length.
pairing: Roast lamb, duck breast or a hard cheese.
drink_window: Now, or cellar a few years
sommelier_note: The generous vintage of the three we carry: hand-harvested by parcel and aged 12 to 14 months in French oak.

title: Pessac-Léognan Rouge
notes: Black fruit, cherry and plum. Silky, velvety, fresh and well balanced.
pairing: Roast lamb, duck breast or a hard cheese.
drink_window: Now, or cellar a few years
sommelier_note: Gold medal at the Lyon International Competition 2022, and one star in the Hachette guide 2023.

title: Saint-Émilion Grand Cru
grape: Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère
notes: Mostly Merlot from clay, sand and red gravel, aged 16 months in barrel, 70 percent new.
pairing: Roast lamb, duck or a mushroom risotto.
drink_window: Also available in the 2020 and 2021 vintages
sommelier_note: A vineyard first planted in the 17th century: 14.5 hectares, picked by hand into crates and sorted twice before it reaches the vat.

title: Graves Blanc
notes: Lively and dry, with citrus, a granitic edge and a surprisingly full palate.
pairing: Seafood and grilled fish, or on its own as an aperitif. Serve at 6–8°C.
sommelier_note: A family estate on a gravel plateau in Budos, 40 km south-east of Bordeaux. Seventy percent Sémillon, aged on its fine lees.

title: Le Charme, Haut-Médoc
notes: Leather, smoke, juniper and grilled pepper, then plum jam. Rich, fresh tannin and a white-pepper finish.
pairing: Partridge in a casserole with fondant potatoes.
drink_window: Now: a mature wine. Serve at 16°C and decant at the table
sommelier_note: A 1999 from one of the most decorated estates in the Haut-Médoc, tasted by the château in 2014 as dominated by the delicacy of its tannins.

title: Aurore de Dauzac Margaux
notes: Garnet with purple tints. Delicate, slightly floral red fruit; round and supple with refined black fruit.
pairing: White meat, poultry, red meat and cheese.
drink_window: At its best 3 to 15 years from the vintage; keeps 15 to 20
sommelier_note: Certified vegan Margaux, picked by hand and aged 12 months in French oak, two-thirds of it new.

title: Montagne-Saint-Émilion
notes: Toasty oak, plum, blackberry and mild spice. Medium-bodied and silky, with a sour-cherry finish.
pairing: Red meat, lamb, chicken and game.
sommelier_note: In the Moze-Berthon family since 1880, on land above 300-year-old stone quarries: hence the name Rocher.

title: Saint-Émilion Grand Cru
notes: Deep cherry-red. Black fruit and light toast; a silky attack and a long, harmonious finish.
pairing: Roast beef, duck or mushrooms.
sommelier_note: Just 1.26 hectares of Saint-Émilion Grand Cru, harvested by hand by a family that has made wine here since 1820.

title: Pomerol
notes: Black fruit, blueberry and morello cherry with a hint of mint. Dense, fresh and silky.
pairing: Beef tenderloin, lamb or a truffle dish.
drink_window: Built to age; decant when young
sommelier_note: A hectare and a half of Pomerol, about 6,000 bottles a year, made entirely in new barrels with Hubert de Boüard of Château Angélus consulting since 2014.

title: Charme de Villars, Fronsac
notes: Round and supple Merlot: fine, elegant and charming young.
pairing: Charcuterie, cheese and easy evenings. Serve at 16°C.
sommelier_note: The prelude to Château Villars: only 8,868 bottles, all Merlot, given the same barrels and care as the grand vin.

title: Fronsac
notes: Floral, peppery and lightly toasted. Smooth, with spicy, roasted flavours and a long finish.
pairing: Roast meats and game. Serve at 16°C.
drink_window: The estate suggested 2016 to 2024: drink now
sommelier_note: One star in the Guide Hachette 2016. Thierry Gaudrie's family has farmed this estate for two centuries.

title: Fronsac
notes: A sunlit vintage: a long warm summer and a calm harvest picked day by day as the grapes ripened.
pairing: Beef, lamb or game birds. Serve at 16°C.
sommelier_note: Yves Beck 93–94, and a wine to watch for Jane Anson in Decanter. The estate ranks 2018 with 2010 and 2005.

title: Petit Chablis
notes: Pale gold. Lively and expressive, with fine minerality and freshness.
pairing: Aperitif, shellfish and seafood, salads and cold cuts. Serve at 10–12°C.
sommelier_note: Kimmeridgian clay and limestone full of marine fossils, native yeasts when the vintage allows, nine months on fine lees.

title: Chablis
notes: Golden and clear. White flowers, fresh fruit and minerality.
pairing: Seafood, snails, sushi, fish, poultry, goat cheese and ham. Serve at 10–12°C.
sommelier_note: Vines averaging 35 years old, a long rest on fine lees, bottled at the estate.

title: Chablis 1er Cru Vaillons
notes: Gold with green glints. White flowers and a green, vegetal edge; ample and supple.
pairing: Pike-perch in beurre blanc, poultry with morels, goat cheese. Serve at 10–12°C.
sommelier_note: South and south-east facing Premier Cru on Kimmeridgian soil, matured long on its fine lees.

title: Pommard
notes: Garnet with purple glints. Blackberry, blueberry, spice, leather and a hint of undergrowth. Powerful and long.
pairing: Grilled red meat, game in sauce, boeuf bourguignon.
drink_window: Now, or cellar a few years
sommelier_note: Hand-harvested into crates and aged 12 months in barrel: Pommard with real structure.

title: Touraine Sauvignon
notes: Pale gold. Floral and citrus; lively, fresh and aromatic.
pairing: Asparagus, oysters, cockles with parsley butter. Serve at 9–11°C.
sommelier_note: Sauvignon on flint, fermented cold and rested a month on its lees.

title: La Storia Zinfandel
notes: Dark cherry, blueberry and plum, with vanilla, cinnamon and a little smoke. Soft tannin, juicy finish.
pairing: Barbecue, burgers, pizza and most of your favourite dishes.
drink_window: Now; even better in 2 to 5 years
sommelier_note: Alexander Valley estate fruit, picked just before the 2019 fires and aged 14 months in American and French oak.

title: La Storia Petite Sirah
notes: Inky. Blueberry, blackberry, cocoa and brown sugar; full-bodied with surprisingly soft tannin.
pairing: Braised short rib and smoked meats.
drink_window: At its best in 5 to 8 years
sommelier_note: Built to last: winemaker Miro Tcholakov calls longevity this grape's great virtue.

title: La Storia Cuvée 32
notes: Cherry, cassis, plum and pomegranate; herbs and spice, then cocoa, cinnamon and licorice.
pairing: Italian food: ragù, pizza, grilled sausages.
sommelier_note: Trentadue's Super Tuscan from Sonoma: Sangiovese and Montepulciano grown in Alexander Valley. The 21st vintage, and the winery's best seller.

title: Thistle & Thorn Cabernet Sauvignon
notes: Ripe plum, blueberry and a hint of leather; blackberry, blackcurrant and toasty oak. Full-bodied.
pairing: Steak or braised short rib.
drink_window: Decant and drink now, or cellar
sommelier_note: Classic, full-bodied Napa Cabernet from the Juliana Vineyard. The tasting notes are the estate's for 2019; we carry the 2022.

title: Napa Valley Chardonnay
notes: Fruit and minerality first, then integrated French oak; a full mid-palate and a crisp, lingering finish.
pairing: Lobster, roast chicken or a creamy pasta.
sommelier_note: Hyde and Stagecoach vineyards, only 25 percent malolactic, ten months on the lees. Just 430 cases made.

title: Napa Valley Syrah
notes: Black cherry, blueberry compote, olives, herbs, peppered salami and violets. Full and seductive.
pairing: Lamb, grilled sausages, peppered salami.
sommelier_note: 94 points from The Wine Advocate.

title: Napa Valley Malbec
notes: Black and blue fruit, white pepper, violets, vanilla and toasty oak; a round, fleshy finish.
pairing: Grilled steak with chimichurri.
sommelier_note: Hillside blocks in the eastern Vaca range, 20 months in mostly new French oak. Only 331 cases.

title: O.P.C. Napa Valley Red
notes: Cassis, violets, tobacco, graphite and peppery herbs. Focused, fresh and long.
pairing: Ribeye or braised beef.
drink_window: Better with 2 to 3 years; keeps a decade
sommelier_note: 92+ from Jeb Dunnuck, and 92 from both The Wine Advocate and Vinous.

title: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
notes: Cassis, black cherry, incense, dark chocolate and toffee. Deep mid-palate, long finish.
pairing: Dry-aged steak.
sommelier_note: 95+ from The Wine Advocate. Howell Mountain and Coombsville hillsides, bottled unfined and unfiltered. 549 cases.

title: Facets Cabernet Sauvignon
notes: Concentrated and rich: raspberry and cassis, cloves and cocoa, soft tannin and a long finish.
pairing: Steak.
sommelier_note: Made by Thomas Rivers Brown and aged 20 months in 80 percent new French oak. 500 cases.

title: Private Reserve Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon
notes: Deep garnet. Bold black fruit and black licorice; velvety tannin and a lively finish.
pairing: Prime rib.
sommelier_note: Eighteen barrels, individually numbered bottles, and 93 points from Wilfred Wong.

title: Arcos da Vinha Reserva Dão
grape: Touriga Nacional, Jaen, Tinta Roriz, Alfrocheiro
notes: Deep ruby. Young, ripe red fruit and wild berries; elegant, smooth and rounded.
pairing: Meat, game, cheese and cured meats. Decant, and serve at 16–18°C.
drink_window: Ready now, with room to age
sommelier_note: Classic Dão freshness and minerality with a modern touch, and the best value on our list.

title: Amaro
notes: Herbal and round: wet leaves, buds and soft fruit, with a light citrus finish.
pairing: After dinner, or in a classic cocktail.
sommelier_note: A single alcohol infusion in the old monks' way, from linden, mulberry, cypress, orange, rhubarb and currant.

title: Grappa Primitivo di Manduria Riserva
notes: Deep amber. Berries, blackberry jam, raisins and toast; elegant and persistent.
pairing: Milk chocolate, cream desserts and dried fruit, or young cheese with honey and mostarda. Serve at 18–20°C.
sommelier_note: Primitivo skins from Puglia, distilled by the de Varda steam method and aged in oak, acacia and cherry.

title: Trié Grappa Riserva
grape: Teroldego, Pinot Bianco and Müller Thurgau skins
notes: Fresh bread, orange zest, wild flowers, elderflower and vanilla, finishing on almond and chocolate.
pairing: Milk chocolate, cream desserts and dried fruit, or young cheese with honey and mostarda. Serve at 18–20°C.
sommelier_note: Aged in oak, acacia and cherry barriques. Also made in 20 cl, 150 cl and 300 cl.

title: Grappa 12 Generazioni Gran Riserva
notes: Gran Riserva grappa finished in oak casks that held Glenfarclas Speyside whisky.
pairing: On its own, after dinner.
sommelier_note: Six generations of Dolzan grappa distillers and six of Grant whisky distillers: a limited edition from both families.

title: Grappa Pinot Nero Riserva Single Cask
notes: Morello cherry, blackcurrant and ripe red fruit with floral and toasted notes. Smooth and rich.
pairing: Milk chocolate, shortbread, cured meats and aged cheese with honey.
sommelier_note: From a single oak barrique, numbered by hand and presented in a gift box.

title: Grappa Stravecchia Selezione Luigi Dolzan
grape: Teroldego, Pinot Nero and Moscato Giallo skins
notes: Bread, orange zest, raisins and amaretto, then vanilla, almond, walnut, chocolate and licorice.
pairing: Milk chocolate and butter pastry, or a plate of salumi and aged cheese.
sommelier_note: Limited production, aged for many years in oak, acacia and cherry, and presented in a mahogany box.

title: Grappa Vecchia Riserva Vibrazioni
notes: Toasted almond, cocoa, vanilla, wisteria, prune and blueberry, with a light finish of spruce resin.
pairing: Chocolate and nut pastries, spiced dishes and braises.
sommelier_note: Aged in spruce barrels from the Fiemme valley, and boxed with a CD of Paganini played on a 1695 Stradivari.

title: Grappa Stravecchia Anniversario
notes: Raisins, tangerine jam, candied citrus and pastry, with spiced vanilla and coffee.
pairing: A good cigar and an evening to yourself.
sommelier_note: Presented in a gift box with the book of the Dolzan family's history.

title: La Grappa 903 Barrique
notes: Delicate and spicy with ripe fruit; soft, balanced and long.
pairing: After dinner, at room temperature.
sommelier_note: Dedicated to founder Bonaventura Maschio, born in 1903, and rested at least six months in barrique. Also in 35 cl, 1 L and 3 L.

title: La Grappa 903 Tipica
notes: Intensely fruity and floral, with honey and fresh herbs. Full and traditional.
pairing: At room temperature, or slightly chilled.
sommelier_note: A clear grappa rested six months in tank, then lightly chilled and filtered before bottling.

title: Amaro Bonaventura Erbe e Fiori
notes: Cornflower, rose and linden with citrus. Pleasantly bitter, with apple and pear at the close.
pairing: At room temperature, or very cold.
sommelier_note: A fresh take on the distillery's old Amaro Bonaventura: geranium, rosewood, nettle, bogbean, orange and citron.

title: Tiramisù di Casa
notes: Cocoa and coffee with sweet vanilla cream. Contains milk and egg.
pairing: On the rocks, or dusted with cocoa.
sommelier_note: Italy's favourite dessert as a liqueur. Allergens: milk and egg.
